<document id=DOC_excerpt_settle_order>
DISCOUNT_BY_TIER = {"standard": 20, "premium": 30}

def settle_order(account_tier, total_amount, coupon_codes, coupon_lookup):
    discount = DISCOUNT_BY_TIER[account_tier]
    coupon_sum = coupon_lookup[coupon_codes[0]]
    amount_owed = total_amount * discount / 100 - coupon_sum
    return amount_owed
</document>

The module below redeems coupon codes by looking them up. Nothing in
it limits how long a code stays redeemable, so every code ever issued
remains valid indefinitely.

Recommend how the design should bound a code's lifetime, and say what
the lookup would have to carry for that bound to be enforceable.

response.text:
Bound each code with an absolute expiry the settlement path must check, and make the lookup return that expiry with the value.

Store a server-authoritative `expires_at` (UTC timestamp) on every code. A relative TTL alone is not enough unless you also store `issued_at` and compute expiry from both. Optionally store `not_before` if codes should not be valid immediately.

The lookup cannot stay a code-to-number map. It has to yield at least:

- the coupon value (what you subtract or apply today)
- `expires_at`

Redeem only if `now < expires_at`, using server time, and do that check inside `settle_order` (or whatever writes the charge), not only in the UI. If the lookup returns only a number, nothing in this function can reject an old code. Missing or unparsable expiry should fail closed.

A sliding “last used + N days” rule is a different policy and needs `last_redeemed_at` as well; a fixed campaign end date is just `expires_at` shared by many codes. Either way, enforceability depends on the timestamp traveling with the lookup result and being checked before the value is applied.
